payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_qualify.py::test_a_layer_whose_record_cannot_be_used_keeps_the_packaged_heads_check stayed green with the spec's wrong version "The record is bound when any `RecordAppend` after its hash line carries the layer's key, so the trailing reconcile line binds the other task's record and the concern its review commit rewrote takes the tree's reason." applied to saffron/qualify.py as an edit. The claim was "A layer with in-cell concerns whose record cannot be used keeps the drop from the packaged head to the graded head as before. It calls `note` once, with `reviewed_diff`, `False`, and `<spec id>: <cause>, so its in-cell concerns are checked from the packaged head`. The witness drives six causes on the stacked layer, each in its own tree, while the unstacked layer's record stays bound. The causes are `no reviewed-diff.json`, and `reviewed-diff.json is unreadable` for a truncated file. They go on with `its sha256 does not match its diff` and `no REVIEW line binds it to this task`. The last two are `the mirror lacks its tree base <sha>` and `its diff does not apply to <sha>`. In the other task's case, a `RecordAppend` under the layer's own key ends the log, as `saffron reconcile` writes one long after the task. In each case two of the stacked layer's concerns are `unverified` with the packaged head's reason, two stay `qualified`, and the only note is the stacked layer's.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
